title: Change Weaver software and contracts
summary: Modify Weaver code, five-stage narrative workflow, Nucleus integration, state, recovery, installation, or public behavior.
use_when: Weaver code, tests, CLI, repository contract, five-stage pipeline, validation, Nucleus requester boundary, private state, activation, maintenance, packaging, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary narrative building or operation of the installed Weaver product.
The proposed feature is live job search, browser automation, application submission, publication, public-profile editing, or another workflow Weaver does not currently implement.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal tested Weaver change whose product and operational documentation match the implementation and whose repository, Nucleus, recovery, privacy, and installation authorities remain explicit.
effects: Modifies Weaver source, tests, authored contracts, documentation, or packaging.
Requester-boundary changes may alter retained prompt content, permissions, correlations, compatibility, recovery, or deployment ordering and require corresponding Nucleus contract work.
Release and deployment remain separate actions that can commit, tag, push, replace installed selectors, or affect an active workflow.
authority: Weaver owns its current workflow, stage order, repository I/O, validation, cancellation intent, recovery, and installation behavior.
The narrative repository owns authored inputs and generated-output validity; Nucleus owns shared execution, authentication, and raw job history.
Weaver must not acquire publication, job-application, public-profile, or browser-workflow authority through an implementation shortcut.
success: The smallest owning Weaver component and every affected exact document agree.
Requester, state, activation, cancellation, validation, maintenance, packaging, rollback, and privacy proofs are updated in proportion to the changed boundary.
failure_and_recovery: Preserve a successfully written stage output even if a later stage or Nucleus runtime operation fails.
Do not add a direct-Codex fallback or a second repository-I/O process lineage to work around readiness or macOS file access.
Persistent or deployment changes require atomic replacement, tamper detection, rollback proof, and an explicit post-commit maintenance recovery path.
privacy: Tests, current state, Nucleus jobs, and diagnostics may contain complete narrative inputs, prompts, or generated outputs and must remain inside their private boundaries.
Release bundles contain only program, deployment, and Chancery documentation bytes, never narrative repository inputs.
steps: Read Weaver's `AGENTS.md` and the exact architecture, CLI, installation, and narrative-repository contracts for the affected behavior.

Before changing the Nucleus requester contract, persistent operational state, service lifecycle, deployment, or compatibility boundary, run `/Users/joey/.local/bin/nucleus manual` and identify the owning authority.
Implement the smallest change and update Weaver's operator-facing documentation in the same change whenever an operational fact changes.
Run `./ci.sh` and the exact deployment, recovery, or requester proofs affected by the change.
Treat release publication and installed deployment as separate actions requiring explicit authorization.
checkpoints: The change remains a narrative workflow feature rather than an unsupported job-application or public-service workflow.
The detached interactive-lineage worker remains the sole repository reader and writer, and Codex still receives only explicitly embedded inputs under its documented permissions.
Current-state and terminal-run semantics remain recoverable without automatic replacement model attempts.
CI passes, and release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Use the current version-matched Nucleus manual for shared requester and compatibility facts rather than assuming source or installed releases move in lockstep.
Scale tests and canaries to the actual change; repository validation, requester execution, worker activation, and installer rollback prove different authorities.
stop_when: A proposed change requires browser, computer-use, publication, or job-application behavior outside Weaver's current contract.
An incompatible requester or persistent-state change lacks migration, rollback, and recovery decisions.
The macOS repository-access boundary cannot be preserved with the interactive caller's process lineage.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying Weaver or cancelling an active installed workflow.
Adding live job search, application submission, publication, profile editing, or volatile UI automation.

consumers.statement: An interactive developer authorized to change the Weaver repository may use this operation for Weaver-owned source, tests, contracts, state, requester integration, recovery, packaging, or documentation.
Ordinary Weaver operation, release publication, deployment, workflow cancellation, job application, browser automation, publication, and profile editing are not implied by this operation.

preconditions.statement: The developer has current Weaver source, applicable Semantics and installed contract context, the exact affected product and narrative-repository documents, and authority for the requested change.
Requester, persistent-state, lifecycle, deployment, or compatibility changes first consult the current Nucleus manual and establish migration, recovery, and coordinated owner obligations.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested scoped change, Weaver source and tests, exact architecture, CLI, installation and selected narrative-repository contracts, installed Nucleus contracts, and authorized compatibility constraints.
A proposed shortcut cannot supply browser, public-service, repository access from Codex, direct-Codex fallback, or automatic model-retry authority.

outputs.statement: The output is the smallest coherent Weaver source and documentation change with proportional tests for requester, state, activation, cancellation, validation, maintenance, packaging, rollback, and privacy boundaries and a passing product CI gate.
This operation does not itself publish, tag, push, deploy, cancel an active run, generate a narrative, or interact with a public service.

data_semantics.statement: Weaver remains a five-stage durable narrative requester: it owns workflow state and repository I/O, the narrative repository owns authored and current output meaning, and Nucleus owns model execution and raw job history.
Nucleus completion is not Weaver success, generated text is not factual authority, and a failed or lost terminal run never implies another model attempt.

identity_and_units.statement: Weaver package and provider release, entry contract version, private-state format, run and stage job IDs, repository contract, and Nucleus protocol or schema versions evolve as distinct identities.
The development operation publishes no effort, schedule, cost, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion requires every affected owning component and exact product or repository document to agree, proportional authority and recovery tests to pass, and Weaver's complete product CI gate to succeed.
The current version-matched Nucleus manual is used for shared requester facts instead of assuming source and installed releases move together.
Passing source tests alone does not establish a released, deployed, runtime-ready, narratively valid, or externally published result.

access.statement: The operation uses the interactive developer's authorized local filesystem and shell for scoped Weaver repository work and exact validation.
It grants no narrative publication, browser, public-profile, job-application, Nucleus credential, active-workflow cancellation, release, or installed-state authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Changes preserve atomic current-state replacement, one-attempt correlations, interactive-lineage repository I/O, terminal-run semantics, maintenance ordering, content-addressed releases, and pre-commit rollback.
Incompatible requester or persistent-state changes version immutable schemas or formats and retain recovery for historical and post-commit states rather than editing them in place.

operational_limits.statement: The operation is limited to the smallest Weaver-owned change and stops at an unsupported product boundary, unresolved owner contract, unsafe migration, or unauthorized release, deployment, cancellation, or public-service effect.
No development duration, review turnaround, release cadence, deployment schedule, or future platform support objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 requires synchronized package and provider release changes, versioned incompatible requester or state changes, exact documentation updates, and rollback proof before retirement.
Release publication and installed deployment remain separate explicitly authorized actions even when their source workflows change.
No universal support window or deprecation period for Weaver releases, state, repositories, Nucleus versions, or macOS behavior is promised.

reliances.statement: Changes to Weaver's requester boundary rely on Nucleus's dedicated integration contract for execution ownership, immutable registrations, correlation, recovery, privacy, and compatibility obligations.

Changes to repository selection, inputs, output validity, or editorial meaning rely on the selected narrative repository's authored contract, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that promise.
The documentation dependency on weaver.workflow.operate is not reinterpreted as a separate external runtime reliance.
Weaver development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
